rows: Record Q2 - total sales $65.1M (+117%), highest growth rate in company history; domestic +157%.
Fitness and vending channels rebounded post-COVID with triple-digit growth, together contributing ~$4.9M incremental revenue.
Management framed quarter as 'another inflection point'; reaffirmed Q1 2021 as the margin low point with sequential improvement expected toward FY2020 levels.
Aluminum can shortage persists industry-wide; ~50% of 2021 cans imported/wrapped, shifting to domestic in back-half 2021 / 2022 to improve margins.
Six-regional warehouse 'orbit' model build-out underway to reduce miles on cans and better service distributors.
Significant inventory build drove a $30.3M six-month operating cash outflow (would have been +$15.1M ex-inventory).
June 9 equity offering generated $67.8M net proceeds for the company; earmarked for working capital, cooler program, warehouse/distribution expansion.
DSD transition characterized as 'fairly neutral' on margin with offsetting synergies; scale efficiencies a future margin opportunity.
Coke Energy delisting is freeing shelf space the team is aggressively pursuing; larger resets expected in 2022.
Amazon EU launch (UK and Germany) in back-half 2021 viewed primarily as brand 'air cover' for broader European retail/distributor expansion.
Pack-size strategy shifting from single-can trial toward take-home four-packs / multipacks (four-packs into Target) to lift velocity.
Strengthening US dollar versus the euro flagged by CFO as a forward margin variable.
Consumer loyalty cited as a key competitive advantage; pricing opportunity seen at scale but watching Monster and using promotional allowances.
Production over the prior two months exceeded all of 2020; nine active co-packers deemed sufficient for the next 12 months.
Renewed COVID variant risk to fitness/vending channels acknowledged as 'definitely a concern.'
Ernst & Young appointed as corporate auditors beginning Q3 2021.
Will significant fall catch-up shelf resets accelerate distribution gains, or has Celsius already captured most reset upside leaving growth on its current path?

Added ~20,000 stores in H1 reaching the 100,000-door milestone; Coke Energy delisting is freeing shelf space the aggressive team is pursuing. Reset timing was COVID-distorted; expects additional distribution gains in Q3 and larger resets in 2022, with DSD activation in small-format/independents a major opportunity. Doors continue growing, though not necessarily at the same rate.
More detail on the planned Amazon Europe launches - market size and expected revenue contribution.

Launching UK and Germany in Q3. Amazon energy drink market in Europe is smaller than the US; anticipates incremental revenue but views the launch primarily as 'air cover' / brand exposure as Celsius seeks retail and distributor partners. Top-line contribution to 'see how it prevails.'
Gross Margin Recovery & DSD Margin Impact
Does confidence in margin recovery mean a return to the prior-year ~47% level, and is the improvement a full-year or exit-rate figure? Does the DSD shift drag on margins?

Expects sequential H2 improvement but cited freight volatility and cycling of imported cans/raw materials as pressures into Q4; set ~43% Q2 gross profit as the expected floor. CFO added EUR/USD parity as a forward variable. DSD transition gives up some top-line dollars/margin but is offset by synergies - 'fairly neutral' - with scale efficiencies a future opportunity.
How is management thinking about pricing in the energy category and Celsius's ability to take price given strong consumer loyalty?

Consumer loyalty is extremely high - a competitive advantage. Sees pricing opportunities as Celsius grows at scale but is currently watching other players (including Monster) and managing promotional allowances to mitigate frontline price increases.
European Channel Expansion, Coolers, Fill Rates & Four-Pack Launch
Plans for Western Europe channels beyond Amazon? Color on the cooler program for the back half? Steady-state fill rates (80% then 90%)? Detail on the four-pack launch?

Channel expansion beyond Amazon is a 'massive opportunity' under discussion; Amazon is the first step. ~500 coolers placed as of June 30 with strong velocity/ROI; more in H2 and 2022 including larger-retailer programs. Fill rates: Q1 ~80%, June ~90%, Q2 avg ~93-94%. More four-packs/multipacks coming in H2 2021 and 2022 to lift velocity.
CVS/7-Eleven DSD Progress & COVID Risk to Fitness/Vending
Update on CVS and 7-Eleven DSD conversion progress; any anticipated impact on fitness/vending channels from the COVID resurgence?

7-Eleven West Coast division converted; Southeast and other regions in progress. CVS conversion ongoing zone-by-zone, working through Anheuser-Busch alcohol-distributor nuances. Fitness/vending have not slowed yet, but renewed COVID is 'definitely a concern' - taking additional safety protocols; 'I don't have a great answer on that.'
More color on branded-cooler metrics - velocity/sell-through with a cooler versus before; are the current nine co-packers sufficient for the 6-12 month plan?

Cooler success is about retail execution - expanding DSD support and field marketing teams, targeting three placements per store and cold/end-cap placement, driving incremental velocity. Nine active co-packers solidify growth for the next 12 months; always seeking more partners. Production over the prior two months exceeded all of 2020.
